=================== #23
Expand/Implement functionality for keyboard navigation/shortcuts
labels: scope: large  milestone: none  assignees: 

### What problem would this solve?

In the current Gitea version there are some shortcuts that can be used for writing comments and navigating the interface, however these are in no way comprehensive, while also lacking a centralized interface of display.

Matching issue on actual Gitea Project: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/5796

### What do you propose?

Implement shortcuts matching Github and have them be accessible from the shortcut of `?`.

=================== #57
`?` opens a shortcut help dialog built from the registry
labels: enhancement, scope: medium, Deferred  milestone: none  assignees: 

> Sub-issue of #23 · **P1** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #56

## User Story
As a user who suspects Gitea has keyboard shortcuts but cannot find them, I want to press `?` on
any page and see every available shortcut grouped by area, so that I can learn them without
reading the source or the docs.

## User Scenario
A user is looking at an issue. They press `?`. A dialog opens in the centre of the page titled
"Keyboard shortcuts", listing the shortcuts under headings such as "Site-wide" and "Repository",
each row showing the keys as `<kbd>` elements next to a description. Focus moves into the dialog;
Tab cycles inside it and does not reach the page behind. They press Escape, the dialog closes, and
focus returns to where it was.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given any page with focus on the document body, when the user presses `?`, then a
      dialog opens listing one row per shortcut registered in #56, with the keys and the
      description.
- [ ] AC2: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Escape, then it closes and focus
      returns to the element that was focused before it opened.
- [ ] AC3: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Tab repeatedly, then focus stays inside
      the dialog and never lands on a control on the page behind it.
- [ ] AC4: Given focus is in a comment textarea, when the user types `?`, then a literal `?` is
      inserted and the dialog does not open.
- [ ] AC5: Given a new shortcut is registered with a description and a category, when the dialog
      is opened, then it appears under that category with no change to the dialog's own code.
- [ ] AC6: Given the page is served in a non-English locale, when the dialog is opened, then the
      title and every description are rendered from locale keys, not hard-coded English.
- [ ] AC7: A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1, AC2 and AC4 and passes `assertNoJsError`.

## Out of Scope
- Adding shortcuts. The dialog lists whatever #56's registry holds, which at merge time is `s`,
  `t` and `?` itself.
- Editing or remapping a shortcut from the dialog.
- The opt-out checkbox — that is #60.
- A printable or documentation-page version of the list.

## Open Questions
- Should the dialog also be reachable by mouse, from a footer link? Proposed: not in this issue,
  to keep it to one entry point that the e2e test can cover.

## Design Decision
**Decision:** Build the dialog on the native `<dialog>` element with `showModal()`, not on
Fomantic's modal.

**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Fomantic modal via `showFomanticModal` in
`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/modal.ts`, which is what the rest of the codebase uses today.
(b) A plain `<div>` with a hand-written focus trap and backdrop.

**Rationale:** `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` says Fomantic is deprecated and new features
must not be built on it — and given this issue's sibling #25 exists to remove Fomantic for
accessibility reasons, adding a new Fomantic modal to the accessibility feature would be
self-defeating. `showModal()` gives the focus trap (AC3), Escape-to-close (AC2), focus restoration
and `aria-modal` semantics from the browser, so (b) would mean hand-writing behaviour the platform
already gets right, which is exactly the class of bug #25 is about.

**Consequences:** Easier — AC2 and AC3 are largely satisfied by the browser, and the dialog has no
jQuery dependency. Harder — `<dialog>` styling differs from every other modal in Gitea, so the
dialog needs its own CSS and will not automatically match the Fomantic modals around it; the
`::backdrop` pseudo-element in particular needs theming against both light and dark themes.

## Scope
medium (5 points)

=================== #59
`c` focuses the comment editor on issue and PR pages
labels: enhancement, scope: small, Deferred  milestone: none  assignees: 

> Sub-issue of #23 · **P3 — Sprint 2 carryover** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56

## User Story
As a user replying to an issue, I want a single key to jump to the comment box from anywhere on
the page, so that I do not have to scroll to the bottom or Tab through every comment to start
writing.

## User Scenario
A maintainer reads a long issue thread. Instead of scrolling past forty comments, they press `c`.
The page scrolls the comment editor into view and the cursor is in it. They type, realise they
want to re-read something, and press Escape — focus leaves the editor, the text they typed is
still there, and the page has not moved.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given an issue page with a comment editor, when the user presses `c` with focus on the
      document body, then the comment textarea is focused and scrolled into view.
- [ ] AC2: Given the comment editor is focused with text in it, when the user presses Escape, then
      the editor is blurred and its content is left unchanged.
- [ ] AC3: Given an archived repository or a signed-out visitor, where no comment editor is
      rendered, when the user presses `c`, then nothing happens and no error is logged.
- [ ] AC4: Given focus is already inside the comment editor, when the user types `c`, then a
      literal `c` is inserted.
- [ ] AC5: Given #57 is merged, when the help dialog is opened on an issue page, then `c` is
      listed under the issue category.
- [ ] AC6: A Playwright test covers AC1, AC2 and AC4.

## Out of Scope
- The pull request review comment boxes and the inline diff reply boxes.
- Submitting the comment — `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+Enter already does that via
  `initGlobalEnterQuickSubmit` in `web_src/js/features/common-form.ts` and is not touched here.
- Quote-reply (`r` on GitHub) and any other issue-page action key.

## Open Questions
- None.

## Design Decision
**Decision:** Register `c` from the issue feature module and have its handler query for the
comment editor at press time, rather than declaring it in the template with a
`<kbd data-shortcut-keys>` element.

**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Reuse the existing `.global-shortcut-wrapper` + `<kbd>` markup
around the comment editor, exactly as `templates/repo/home_sidebar_top.tmpl` does for `s`.
(b) Register the shortcut only when the editor element is found during page init.

**Rationale:** (a) renders a visible `<kbd>C</kbd>` hint inside the comment box's chrome, which is
the wrong affordance for a box the user is about to type into — the `s` and `t` hints sit in
search inputs where the hint reads as placeholder text. (b) fails on pages where the editor is
added to the DOM later, and Gitea renders the editor lazily in more than one place; querying at
press time makes AC3 a null check instead of an init-order problem.

**Consequences:** Easier — works regardless of when the editor is rendered, and AC3 is a single
early return. Harder — there is no visible hint that `c` exists, so discoverability depends
entirely on the help dialog from #57 shipping too.

## Scope

=================== #60
Character-key shortcuts can be turned off (WCAG 2.1.4)
labels: enhancement, scope: small, Deferred  milestone: none  assignees: 

> Sub-issue of #23 · **P3 — Sprint 2 carryover** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56, #57

## User Story
As a user of speech recognition software, I want to turn off Gitea's single-character shortcuts,
so that dictating a word into the page does not fire a shortcut and navigate me away from what I
was writing.

## User Scenario
Someone using voice control finds that saying a word while the page has focus keeps triggering the
file finder. They press `?`, see a checkbox at the bottom of the shortcut dialog reading "Enable
character key shortcuts", and clear it. The shortcut list greys out. They close the dialog, dictate
freely, and the setting is still off the next time they open Gitea in that browser.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the shortcut help dialog, when the user clears the "Enable character key
      shortcuts" checkbox, then pressing `s`, `t` or any `g` sequence has no effect.
- [ ] AC2: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user reloads the page, then they are still
      disabled.
- [ ] AC3: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user presses `?`, then the help dialog still
      opens, so the setting can be turned back on without a mouse.
- [ ] AC4: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user re-checks the box, then `s` focuses the
      repo sidebar search again without a reload.
- [ ] AC5: Given shortcuts are disabled, when a shortcut that requires a modifier is pressed, then
      it still runs — only character keys are suppressed.
- [ ] AC6: Given a browser with storage blocked, when the page loads, then shortcuts default to
      enabled and no error is thrown.
- [ ] AC7: Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover AC1, AC3, AC5 and AC6.

## Out of Scope
- Remapping individual shortcuts, or turning off one shortcut at a time.
- Storing the preference on the server or syncing it across devices or browsers.
- A copy of the toggle in the user settings pages.

## Open Questions
- WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.4 is satisfied by "turn off", "remap" or "active on focus only". This issue
  takes "turn off" as the cheapest complete option; confirm that is the team's reading.

## Design Decision
**Decision:** Store the preference in `localStorage` and keep `?` itself exempt from the toggle.

**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A server-side user setting, as a column on the user table with a
checkbox on the appearance settings page. (b) Storing it in `localStorage` but suppressing every
shortcut including `?`.

**Rationale:** (a) needs a migration and a settings form for a preference that is per-browser by
nature — someone using voice control on one machine does not need it off everywhere — and a
migration is more than this issue is worth. (b) is more literally correct against SC 2.1.4, but it
leaves a keyboard-only user who has disabled shortcuts with no keyboard route back to the dialog,
which trades one accessibility failure for another; keeping exactly one exempt key is the standard
escape hatch.

**Consequences:** Easier — no server change, no migration, and the flag is a single module-level
read the registry consults before dispatching. Harder — the preference does not follow the user to
another browser or machine and is invisible to support; and `?` staying live is a documented
deliberate exception that needs a comment in the code so nobody "fixes" it later.

## Scope
small (2 points)

# Course workflow — issues, PRs, reviews, sprint deliverables

Course rules, not upstream Gitea ones. Source: the course site <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>
(Sprints pages) and `docs/sprint0/standards.md`. Everyone on the team, and every AI session, uses
the formats below so all issues and PRs look the same. The GitHub templates in `.github/` carry the
same formats; if they ever disagree with this page, fix the template.

AI disclosure has its own page: `AI-ASSISTANCE.md`.

## Current sprint: Sprint 1

- **Dates:** Sep 22 – Oct 8, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Oct 8, 11:59 PM**.
- **Points:** 100 (10% of the course grade).
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D6) or no release (D7) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** every Sprint 0 standard and convention still applies.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 1` milestone with every selected issue on it | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), peer-reviewed by a teammate | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue | 7 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs | 36 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 7 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint1/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | Sprint report | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint1/report.md` |
| D7 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s1` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D8 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Every issue has exactly **one** assignee. Specs should be final by
  Sep 27.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. The folder must exist even if no AI was used. In
  that case, post an issue comment saying so. Log links go in **issue comments only**, never in PRs
  (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D7:** keep Sprint 0's base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s0` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s1`), push the tag
  to origin, and write release notes listing the features, fixes and improvements.
- **Reviews:** each student reviews at least one PR per sprint. Over the semester, each student
  reviews every teammate at least once.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR accepted by upstream Gitea.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once it is approved, every review comment is addressed and CI
passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), is on the sprint milestone, and has its AI
Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Issue format: feature (user story)

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/user-story.yaml`. The user story must meet INVEST: Independent,
Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

```markdown
## User Story
As a <role>, I want <capability> so that <benefit>.

## User Scenario
<A short concrete walk-through: who, where in the UI, what they do, what they see.>

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given <state>, when <action>, then <observable result>.
- [ ] AC2: ...
- [ ] AC3: ...            (at least 3; each has a clear pass/fail result)

## Out of Scope
- <What this issue deliberately does not do.>

## Open Questions
- <Unresolved questions, or "None".>

## Design Decision
**Decision:** <what was chosen>
**Alternatives Considered:** <at least one other option>
**Rationale:** <why this one>
**Consequences:** <trade-offs, follow-up work, what it makes harder>

## Scope
small | medium | large, and matching `scope:` label
```

## Issue format: bug report

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yaml`.

```markdown
## Observed Behavior
## Expected Behavior
## Steps to Reproduce
1. ...
## Additional Information
<Version or commit, browser/OS, logs, screenshots.>
## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.>
```

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Peer review (D2):** a teammate reads the spec and comments `Spec reviewed — <notes>` on the
  issue before implementation starts.

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality 4, CI or manual verification 3, review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
```

## Sprint report (D6) sections

`docs/sprint<N>/report.md`, following `docs/sprint0/report.md`:

- Team: names, GitHub usernames, project name, repository link.
- Sprint overview.
- Backlog: milestone link, plus a table of title, owner, points, scope and status.
- Requirements and design: when specs were done, what surprised you, design rationale.
- Completed issues: title, owner, PR link, author, reviewer, what changed.
- Test strategy, including untestable changes and why.
- AI tool usage per member: tools, session count, AI log folder link, and 2–3 sentences on lessons
  learned.
- Release: tag and release link.
- Risks and retrospective: what worked, what slowed the team down, Sprint 2 changes.
- Sprint 2 plan: initial ideas and carryover issues.

import {isDocumentFragmentOrElementNode} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import type {Promisable} from '../types.ts';
import type {InitPerformanceTracer} from './init.ts';
import {initAriaLabels} from './fomantic/base.ts';

let globalSelectorObserverInited = false;

type SelectorHandler<T extends Element> = {selector: string, handler: (el: T) => void};
const selectorHandlers: SelectorHandler<Element>[] = [];

type GlobalEventFunc<T extends HTMLElement, E extends Event> = (el: T, e: E) => Promisable<void>;
const globalEventFuncs: Record<string, GlobalEventFunc<HTMLElement, Event>> = {};

type GlobalInitFunc<T extends Element> = (el: T) => Promisable<void>;
const globalInitFuncs: Record<string, GlobalInitFunc<Element>> = {};

// It handles the global events for all `<div data-global-click="onSomeElemClick"></div>` elements.
export function registerGlobalEventFunc<T extends HTMLElement, E extends Event>(event: string, name: string, func: GlobalEventFunc<T, E>) {
  globalEventFuncs[`${event}:${name}`] = func as GlobalEventFunc<HTMLElement, Event>;
}

// It handles the global init functions by a selector, for example:
// > registerGlobalSelectorObserver('.ui.dropdown:not(.custom)', (el) => { initDropdown(el, ...) });
// ATTENTION: For most cases, it's recommended to use registerGlobalInitFunc instead,
// Because this selector-based approach is less efficient and less maintainable.
// But if there are already a lot of elements on many pages, this selector-based approach is more convenient for exiting code.
export function registerGlobalSelectorFunc<T extends Element>(selector: string, handler: (el: T) => void) {
  selectorHandlers.push({selector, handler: handler as (el: Element) => void});
  // Then initAddedElementObserver will call this handler for all existing elements after all handlers are added.
  // This approach makes the init stage only need to do one "querySelectorAll".
  if (!globalSelectorObserverInited) return;
  for (const el of document.querySelectorAll<T>(selector)) {
    handler(el);
  }
}

// It handles the global init functions for all `<div data-global-int="initSomeElem"></div>` elements.
export function registerGlobalInitFunc<T extends HTMLElement>(name: string, handler: GlobalInitFunc<T>) {
  globalInitFuncs[name] = handler as GlobalInitFunc<Element>;
  // The "global init" functions are managed internally and called by callGlobalInitFunc
  // They must be ready before initGlobalSelectorObserver is called.
  if (globalSelectorObserverInited) throw new Error('registerGlobalInitFunc() must be called before initGlobalSelectorObserver()');
}

function callGlobalInitFunc(el: Element) {
  // TODO: GLOBAL-INIT-MULTIPLE-FUNCTIONS: maybe in the future we need to extend it to support multiple functions, for example: `data-global-init="func1 func2 func3"`
  const initFunc = el.getAttribute('data-global-init')!;
  const func = globalInitFuncs[initFunc];
  if (!func) throw new Error(`Global init function "${initFunc}" not found`);

  // when an element node is removed and added again, it should not be re-initialized again.
  type GiteaGlobalInitElement = Partial<Element> & {_giteaGlobalInited: boolean};
  if ((el as GiteaGlobalInitElement)._giteaGlobalInited) return;
  (el as GiteaGlobalInitElement)._giteaGlobalInited = true;

  func(el);
}

function attachGlobalEvents() {
  // add global "[data-global-click]" event handler
  document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    const elem = (e.target as HTMLElement).closest<HTMLElement>('[data-global-click]');
    if (!elem) return;
    const funcName = elem.getAttribute('data-global-click');
    const func = globalEventFuncs[`click:${funcName}`];
    if (!func) throw new Error(`Global event function "click:${funcName}" not found`);
    func(elem, e);
  });
}

The specs mostly hold up. Three problems span more than one issue, and a handful of gaps in each issue change the design or the ACs. I only read things and changed nothing on GitHub.

## Blocking links and milestone

The current links match what the code needs: #56 blocks #57, #58, #59 and #60, and #57 blocks #60. Two problems:

- **A link is missing.** #58 AC6 and #59 AC5 both test the `?` dialog from #57, but neither is blocked by #57. #57 also has no owner and no milestone, so if nobody takes it, #58 AC6 can't be checked this sprint. Your options:
  - (a) Drop #58 AC6, and add "lists any `g` chords on the page" to #57's ACs. I recommend this because #58 then doesn't wait on #57.
  - (b) Mark #58 as blocked by #57.
  - (c) Get a teammate to claim #57.
- **#56 isn't on the Sprint 2 milestone.** Only #58 is, and #58 can't merge without #56. Both issues still carry the `Deferred` label.

## Do the other shortcut issues actually need #56?

| Issue | Needs #56? |
| --- | --- |
| #57 `?` dialog | Yes. It lists what the registry holds, which is the main reason #56 exists. |
| #58 `g` chords | Yes. It depends on #56's two-key sequences (AC2/AC3). |
| #59 `c` | Only because its design drops the visible `<kbd>` hint. Still valid, just a weaker link than the others. |
| #60 off switch | Yes. It needs a single place where every shortcut runs, so one check can turn them off. |

Going the other way, **#56 AC5 (modifier keys like `mod+k`) has nothing that uses it.** None of the other issues registers a shortcut with a modifier; only #60 AC5 mentions one, as a "what if". Cutting it makes #56 smaller and also settles the `mod` open question. Keeping it prepares for #23's "match GitHub" goal. I'd lean toward cutting it, but it's your call.

## #56: gaps that change the design or ACs

1. **The design decision clashes with AC6 ("a duplicate throws").** Clicking a file in the file tree swaps out the page content (`web_src/js/components/ViewFileTreeStore.ts:45`). That rebuilds the file finder, including a fresh `<kbd data-shortcut-keys="t">`.
   - If each `<kbd>` registers its shortcut when it loads, clicking a second file registers `t` again and throws.
   - The old `t` entry also still points at an input that no longer exists.
   - Today's code avoids this by finding the `<kbd>` at the moment the key is pressed (`shortcut.ts:57`). The decision needs to say how `<kbd>` shortcuts cope with elements that come and go, and AC6 may need to change to match.
2. **Where translated text comes from.** The JavaScript can't look up translations by key. Translated text has to arrive from the server: a `data-locale-*` attribute, `pageData`, or `window.config.i18n` (`.claude-students/docs/i18n.md:34-56`).
   - #56 decides what a shortcut's description and category hold, and #57 AC6 depends on that choice.
   - The `s` and `t` `<kbd>` elements have no description today.
   - If #56 doesn't settle this, #57 will have to change #56's design.
3. **What happens when the second key doesn't match.** The ACs cover `g` plus a matching key, and `g` plus a timeout. They don't cover `g` followed by a key that isn't a registered pair, like `g s`: does `s` still fire, or is it swallowed? This matters once #58's `g c` and #59's `c` are on the same issue page.
4. **Protection against breaking what already works.** AC1 only covers `s`. Two other behaviours live in the same code you're rewriting, and no existing test covers either:
   - the `t` file finder;
   - Escape clearing the input and moving focus out of it (`shortcut.ts:40-47`).

## #58: gaps that change the design or ACs

1. **The title doesn't match the scope.** The title says "repo and global pages", but Out of Scope excludes global chords.
2. **The set of letters isn't consistent.** The scenario uses `g w` (wiki), which AC2 doesn't list, and `g r` is still an open question. AC2 tests the exact list, so it has to be settled.
3. **Repos with an external issue tracker or wiki.** These repos still show an "Issues" tab, but it links to another site in a new tab (`templates/repo/header.tmpl:100-104`; the wiki equivalent is at 156-160). Reading the link off the tab bar would send `g i` to that other site. AC3 doesn't say what should happen here.
4. **Where `g c` goes.** On a non-default branch, the Code tab links to that branch, not the repo's front page (`header.tmpl:87`). AC1 should say which one you want.

Two smaller notes that can wait:
- On narrow screens, tabs that don't fit move into a "more" popup. That popup stays inside `<overflow-menu>` (`overflow-menu.ts:184`), so the selector has to search the whole `<overflow-menu>`, not just `.overflow-menu-items`.
- AC7 needs a new e2e test helper that turns off a repo's issues. `tests/e2e/utils.ts` only has `apiCreateRepo`.

## Fine to fix during the rewrite
- #56's user story is really a developer story ("nothing visible changes"). Making the role the frontend developer, as you did for #53, fits better.
- Some headers are stale: "P2 — only if capacity allows" and "can follow in Sprint 2".
- The footers credit @Jack-Donohue and cite `docs/sprint1/backlog-refinement.md`, which isn't in the repo. Each issue also needs your own AI-assistance section.
- The chord timeout question has to be settled before #56 AC3 can be tested.

```text
=================== #53
A way to store and retrieve "closed" reasons for issues and PRs  [by ab-wm] {enhancement, scope: medium}

### User Story

As a front-end developer, I want a way to store messages detailing issue and PR close reasons in the system so that I can create a display on the front end to show the reason why an issue or PR was closed, but there is no current way to store nor recover the reason behind their closing.

### User Scenario

For a front-end developer to implement the feature, there needs to be a clear way to send and receive information, as it would be ridiculous to expect the front end to directly communicate with the DB. A central function will be implemented along with supporting infrastructure (such as a predefined list and constraints) that the user will need to implement the desired features.

The finer details on _how_ the information is stored by the system is abstracted away, and so, this single set of functionality will permit each storage and retrieval of the issue messages. This will similarly be the user story of how the API will handle the messages.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a database with existing open and closed issues and PRs, when the migration runs, then the close-reason columns exist on the issue table and every existing issue and PR has an empty reason; existing close comments, which have no close-reason metadata, also read as having no reason.
- [ ] AC2: Given an open issue, when it is closed through the close service with a valid reason (completed, not planned, duplicate or other), then both the issue and its new close timeline comment store that reason.
- [ ] AC3: Given the reason "other", when the text is empty or longer than 255 characters, then the close is rejected with its own error and the issue stays open; valid text is stored exactly as entered.
- [ ] AC4: Given the reason "duplicate", when the target number does not exist in the same repository or is the issue itself, then the close is rejected with its own error; a valid target is stored, and the close comment has the target issue loaded (number, title, link).
- [ ] AC5: Given a pull request, when it is closed as "completed", then the close is rejected with its own error; the allowed-reasons list for a PR leaves out "completed" and an issue's list includes all four.
- [ ] AC6: Given an issue closed with a reason, when it is reopened, then the issue's reason is cleared and the earlier close comment keeps its reason.
- [ ] AC7: Given any existing close path (web, bulk, commit keyword, merged PR, branch deletion, API), when it closes an issue without a reason, then the close succeeds as before with an empty reason, and merging a PR still records no reason.



### Out of Scope

UI Displaying of information: Issue (#54 )
API access: Issue (#55 )
Issues for automatic closing of issues and PRs: Issue (#55 )

Other: Note that the pop ups on the UI will not show the reason since the message won't be written to the appropriate JSON field, for now. This will be addressed in the future (issue #55) to avoid touching the API under this issue.

=================== #54
Select close reasons for Issues and PRs and show it under closed Issues and PRs in the UI.  [by ab-wm] {enhancement, scope: medium}

### User Story

As a repository maintainer, I want a way to set a close reason for an issue and a PR so there is historical context for why the closing occurred. Furthermore, I want to be able to clearly and quickly see the reason behind the closing of an issue or PR in the UI.

### User Scenario

#### Writing the Reasons
A user who is attempting to close an issue or PR can either close the issue with a default reason by clicking the current "close issue/PR" button or by clicking the split button that will show a drop down to select from set responses:

| Reason | Special Semantics |
| --- | ---| 
| "Completed" | **Default** option for Issue. **NOT AVAILABLE FOR PR**. |
|"Not Planned" | **Default** for PR |
| "Duplicate" | Asks for the original issue number and links to the relevant issue |
| "Other" | Shows a text box to fill (required, and max 255 characters) (shown in plain text) |

This applies to the issue/PR bulk "Close" action button, but only "completed and not planned" are the possible reasons for issues and "not planned" for PRs.

The button text will reflect the chosen reason.

**Note: The choice/reason can be changed before closing the issue or PR**.

#### Display
Show the reason on the "close timeline comment." Closed items will also show a distinct icon/label per reason for quick visual feedback.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given an open issue, when the user clicks the main Close button without opening the dropdown, then it closes as "Completed"; an open PR closed the same way closes as "Not planned".
- [ ] AC2: Given an open issue, when the user opens the Close button's dropdown, then it offers Completed, Not planned, Duplicate and Other; for a PR it offers the same list without Completed, and merging a PR still needs no reason.
- [ ] AC3: Given a reason picked from the dropdown, when the user picks a different one before closing (with or without a comment typed), then the button text shows the latest choice and that reason is the one saved.
- [ ] AC4: Given "Duplicate" is chosen, when the number entered is not an issue or PR in the same repository, or is the item itself, then the close is refused with an error message and the item stays open; a valid number closes it, and the timeline links to the original.
- [ ] AC5: Given "Other" is chosen, when the text box is empty or longer than 255 characters, then the close is refused with an error message; otherwise the text is saved and the timeline shows it as plain text, with HTML and Markdown not rendered.
- [ ] AC6: Given several open issues selected on the Issues tab, when the user bulk-closes them as Completed or Not planned, then every selected issue closes with that reason; on the Pull Requests tab, the bulk dropdown offers only Not planned.
- [ ] AC7: Given an item closed with a reason, when its timeline is viewed, then the close event states the reason, e.g. "closed this as not planned", "closed this as a duplicate of #N" or "closed this: <text>".
- [ ] AC8: Given closed items with different reasons, when viewed in the issue or PR list and on the item's page, then each reason shows its own icon or label; items closed before this feature, which have no reason, look exactly as they do today.
- [ ] AC9: Given an item closed with a reason, when it is reopened, then the list and page no longer show the reason's icon or label, and the timeline keeps the earlier close event with its reason.
- [ ] AC10: Given the new dropdown, text box, error messages and timeline text, when a page shows them in English, then each string comes from a key in `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`, and no other locale file is changed.


### Out of Scope

- Pop up icon. Will be implemented alongside the API and automated changes in issue #55  since that impacts the API layer.
- Closing reason via Gitea's automated closing services: Same as above, to be implemented in issue #55.

### Open Questions

- ~~Should marking something as duplicate require the user to input a number (with pop ups like in the issues and PR editors), or a drop-down.~~: **Answered by decision 7**

### Scope

medium

=================== #55
Set close reason when issue or PR is closed by an automated system or via API  [by ab-wm] {enhancement, scope: medium}

### User Story

As a repository maintainer whose team relies on scripts and automation, I want every automatic or API close of an issue or PR to record a reason that my tools can set and read back through the API, so that all closing activity can be audited.

### User Scenario

As there are alternative ways to close an issue or PR that is not via the UI, that is, via Gitea's automated closing paths or via an API, these actions either need to be able to set a reason, or fall back onto a default value so closed issues/PRs have an established reason.

#### Automated Closing
Automated closing (Gitea itself) has four distinct pathways that have been found:

| How it closes | Reason |
|---|---|
| Commit message keyword ("fixes #5") | Completed |
| Merged PR that references an issue | Completed (on the referenced issue) |
| PR auto-closed because its head branch was deleted | Not planned |
| PRs auto-closed because the repo's branches were removed | Not planned |

<br>

#### API
Any closing via the API come from scripts and tools that interact with the REST API. As such, there are more technical requirements for them:
- Bad inputs are rejected via a 422 with a message
- Old scripts keep working with a default fallback.
- The issue and PR endpoints accept a close reason when closing.
- Responses from the server will include the new reasons so they can be read by tools or scripts.

#### Extra in scope: Popups
Popups that detail a brief summary of the issue/PR read that information from a JSON. Since modifying this JSON comes under the API's Jurisdiction, this change will be implemented as well.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given an open issue, when a pushed commit's message closes it with a keyword (e.g. "fixes #5"), then it closes as Completed.
- [ ] AC2: Given an open issue referenced by a pull request, when that pull request is merged and closes the issue, then the issue closes as Completed.
- [ ] AC3: Given an open pull request, when its head branch is deleted or the repository's branches are removed, then the pull request closes as Not planned.
- [ ] AC4: Given a script closing an issue or pull request through the API, when it sends a valid close reason, then the item closes with that reason and the timeline shows it.
- [ ] AC5: Given a script closing through the API, when it sends an invalid reason ("other" with no text or more than 255 characters, a duplicate that does not exist in the same repository, or "completed" on a pull request), then the request is rejected with a 422 and a message, and the item stays open.
- [ ] AC6: Given an existing script that closes issues or pull requests through the API without a reason, including creating an issue that starts closed, when it runs unchanged, then it succeeds and the item closes as Completed (issues) or Not planned (pull requests).
- [ ] AC7: Given an issue or pull request closed with a reason, when a tool reads it through the API, then the response includes the reason and any custom text; items without a reason return an empty reason.
- [ ] AC8: Given an item closed with a reason, when a user hovers over a reference to it (e.g. #5), then the popup shows that reason's icon.
- [ ] AC9: Given the API documentation page, when a script writer looks up the issue and pull request endpoints, then the new close reason inputs and response fields are listed.


### Out of Scope

- Showing reasons in UI: Addressed by issue #54. This is the blocker for the Timeline (AC4) and the popup icons/labels that will be needed (AC8)
- Back "dating"/"reasoning" old issues and PRs.

### Open Questions

Should old issues and PRs have a way to be updated? From the perspective of archival, likely not, but is still something to consider. This is, however, out of scope of the current issue but a consequence that should be considered.




### Scope

medium (8 points)

@ab-wm:
# Design decisions for Commit 1 that changed the DB

### Decision 1: `CloseIssue` becomes a wrapper over a new `CloseIssueWithReason`

**Decision:** The close logic moves into a new `CloseIssueWithReason` in `services/issue/status.go`. `CloseIssue` keeps its signature and calls it with an empty reason, with a code comment marking it as a backwards-compatibility step.
**Alternatives Considered:** Change `CloseIssue`'s signature and update all nine call sites.
**Rationale:** Automatic closes (commit keywords, merged PRs, branch deletion) have no reason to give. The wrapper leaves them untouched.
**Consequences:** Two entry points for closing an issue. New code that should record a reason must call `CloseIssueWithReason`; the comment on `CloseIssue` points there.

### Decision 2: Whitespace-only "other" text counts as empty

**Decision:** The "other" text is trimmed before the empty check (AC3).
**Alternatives Considered:** Check the raw text, so any non-empty string, including only spaces, passes.
**Rationale:** Text should be trimmed to avoid blank reason strings.
**Consequences:** Needs its own test case next to the empty-text case.

### Decision 3: Store the reason as a Go integer enum plus two non-null columns

**Decision:** Add three columns to `issue`: `close_reason`, `close_reason_text` and `close_duplicate_issue_id`.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A single `close_reason_text` column holding either a fixed reason or the "other" text. (b) Nullable columns, with NULL meaning no reason. (c) A database-level ENUM type.
**Rationale:** (a) can't tell "other: not planned" apart from the real "not planned." (b) makes every consumer handle NULL, while `NOT NULL DEFAULT` fills existing rows in the same `ALTER TABLE` (c) doesn't exist in Gitea: enums are Go integer types stored as plain integer columns (`CommentType`, `ReviewType`, `XRefAction`), because the four supported databases don't share an ENUM type.
**Consequences:** The database only holds numbers, so the meaning of each value lives in Go and values must never be renumbered. Nothing in the database restricts the values, so validation must reject anything outside the list. The close comment stores its own copy of the reason (Decision 4), so the issue can hold the current reason while each close comment keeps the one it was closed with.

### Decision 4: Close comments store their reason in `CommentMetaData`, not new columns

**Decision:** A close comment's reason, "other" text and duplicate target, go into the existing `CommentMetaData` JSON field instead of new `comment` columns. AC1 is amended to match: the migration only adds columns to `issue`.
**Alternatives Considered:** The same three columns on `comment` as on `issue`, as AC1 was first written.
**Rationale:** The field's own code comment says to put all non-index metadata there (`models/issues/comment.go`, added upstream in #29311), and later features followed it (the CODEOWNERS marker). It holds data that never changes after insert, which is AC6's rule that an earlier close comment keeps its reason.
**Consequences:** SQL can't filter, sort or index comments by close reason: nothing in `models/` queries inside JSON, and the four databases write JSON queries differently. That's acceptable because comments are only read one issue at a time.
-----
@ab-wm:
# Design decisions for Commit 3 that implemented rules in the model layer

**Decision:** Closing with "completed", "not planned", "duplicate" or no reason while also sending text is rejected with `ErrInvalidCloseReasonText`. Whitespace-only text still counts as no text (Decision 2).
**Alternatives Considered:** Silently discard the text and close with the chosen reason.
**Rationale:** A close carries exactly one reason, and text belongs only to "other". A form or API client that sends both has a bug.
**Consequences:** The close form in #54 has to clear the text box when a reason other than "other" is picked, and API clients in #55 get a 400 if they send both.
-----
@ab-wm:
# Design decisions for Commit 8 that implemented the backend half of the web close path

### Decision 6: The web close form carries the reason in this issue; the UI inputs come in #54

**Decision:** The backend half of the web close path is done in #53. `CreateCommentForm` gains the reason fields, and `NewComment` in `routers/web/repo/issue_comment.go` calls `CloseIssueWithReason` and shows a flash message when the reason is refused. #54 only adds the inputs to the template and the display. Bulk close on the issue list (`UpdateIssueStatus`) keeps closing with no reason, and the API stays with #55.
**Alternatives Considered:** Leave the handler on `CloseIssue` and let #54 wire the form, the handler and the template together.
**Rationale:** Reading the request, building `CloseReasonOptions` and turning refusals into a response are server-side work that can be tested by posting the form, with no HTML involved. It also fixes a silent failure: the handler only logs close errors other than open dependencies, so a refused reason would otherwise leave the issue open with no message.
**Consequences:** Until #54 adds the inputs, the form sends no reason and the close button behaves exactly as before. Refusals need a user-visible string in the locale file. Bulk close cannot record a reason.

    const el = e.target as HTMLElement;
    const hasCtrlOrMeta = ((e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) && !e.altKey);
    const isCtrlEnterInTextarea = hasCtrlOrMeta && el.matches('textarea');
    // an input in a normal form could handle Enter key by default, so we only handle the input outside a form
    const isEnterInBareInput = el.matches('input') && !el.closest('form');
    if ((isCtrlEnterInTextarea || isEnterInBareInput) && handleGlobalEnterQuickSubmit(el)) {
      e.preventDefault();
    }
  });
}

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/github/hotkey`

```text
**Declaration:** Hotkeys are read from `data-hotkey` on the element, e.g. `<a data-hotkey="j">`. You can also pass the hotkey to `install(el, hotkeyString)`, which overrides the attribute. Hotkeys are registered with `install()` and removed with `uninstall()`.

**Firing:** The default action depends on the element. Form fields and `contenteditable` elements receive focus. Other elements are clicked. Every element also emits a cancellable `hotkey-fire` event, so you can call `preventDefault()` to replace the default behavior with your own.

**Sequences:** Keys separated by a space form a sequence, such as `g c`. The README says "Two-key-sequences such as `g c` and `g i` are stored under the 'g' key in a nested object." It also notes that `g c` and a bare `g` can't coexist on the same page.

**Chord timeout:** The README gives 1500 ms. While the user has pressed `g`, the `c` hotkey is unavailable until the sequence resolves or the wait ends.

**Form fields:** Form fields are focused when their hotkey fires, not clicked. The README says "The hotkey can be scoped to a form field:" and shows a `data-hotkey-scope` example. It doesn't explain the scoping mechanics beyond that example.

**Mod:** Supported. `"Mod"` maps to `Meta` on macOS/iOS and to `Control` on Windows/Linux. The README also says `"Mod+"` can appear in any position in the string.

**Enumerating registered hotkeys:** The README doesn't document any API for listing or enumerating registered hotkeys. It only shows `install` and `uninstall`.
```

```text
**Summary:** PR #36416 added GitHub-style keyboard shortcuts for repository navigation. `T` focuses the "Go to file" input, `S` focuses "Search code," and `Escape` clears and unfocuses either input. Each search input shows a `kbd` hint that hides when the input is focused or has a value. The PR was merged on February 23, 2026, and closed issue #36417.

**Design:** The first version used hardcoded page logic. After maintainer feedback, the author switched to a declarative approach. Elements declare their shortcut with a `data-global-keyboard-shortcut` attribute, and a central handler in `observer.ts` picks them up, similar to the existing `data-global-init` and `data-global-click` patterns. The final version used a general `global-shortcut-wrapper` and needed no special styles.

**Review discussion relevant to future shortcut work:**

- **Declarative design:** wxiaoguang asked that "the elements declare what keyboard shortcut they support" so the code doesn't have to guess which elements are on the page. He linked issue #5796 as the place where maintainers had discussed shortcuts at length.
- **`aria-keyshortcuts`:** silverwind suggested using the standard attribute, asking "Or maybe even make it work completely off that attribute?" wxiaoguang replied with a screenshot rather than explaining, and the merged code is the answer to that question. The thread doesn't say whether the attribute was used directly.
- **Testing:** silverwind noted that E2E tests don't run in CI and asked how the author ran them. The author pointed to `tests/e2e/README.md`. wxiaoguang also said the unit test "doesn't really test" anything and removed it.

The thread doesn't discuss modifier keys, key combinations or chords, a central shortcut registry, a help dialog, or using a library such as @github/hotkey. Those topics are only referenced through the linked issue #5796, which isn't included here.

It was opened on October 5, 2026, and it was the only PR referenced as fixing issue #5796, "Feature Request: Support keyboard hotkeys in web interface."

**Author's description:** The PR says it fixes #5796. The key line is that "Global shortcuts can be easily introduced by adding "data-shortcut-keys" to the elements." The design is declarative: a shortcut is added by placing a `data-shortcut-keys` attribute on an element, not by registering a handler in code.

**Changes (from the visible file list and commit messages):**
- `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`: shortcut dispatch, key-sequence matching, and the help dialog. The dialog is titled "Keyboard Shortcuts."
- `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts`: tests for shortcut and help behavior.

- `templates/repo/header.tmpl`: repository navigation shortcuts.
- `templates/base/head_navbar_icons.tmpl`: the notifications shortcut.

- Multi-key sequences, such as `g n` for Notifications and `g i` for issues.

- **Modal refactor:** the close-control changes were tied to a separate modal cleanup, PR #39654.
- **Approvals:** delvh, lunny, and bircni approved. The CI checks passed (23 total).

#56 is a frontend-only change: TypeScript in `web_src/js`, with no Go. It doesn't change what users see, but it isn't backend work. I'm reading "draft PR" as a draft of the rewritten issue body; tell me if you meant something else.

## How #56's claims hold up

| Claim | Holds? |
| --- | --- |
| `s` focuses the sidebar search and its `S` hint hides | **Yes.** See `templates/repo/home_sidebar_top.tmpl:4-6` and `shortcut.ts:57-68`. |
| `t` "opens the file finder" | **Partly.** `t` only puts the cursor in the "Go to file" box (`RepoFileSearch.vue:148-154`); the results appear once you type. The box is on the repo home page and the file/folder views. |
| Ctrl/Alt/Cmd are ignored at `shortcut.ts:35`, and the `<kbd>` lookup is at line 57 | **Yes.** |
| The code editor's own key handling stays separate | **Yes.** Its page-wide listener only tracks Ctrl/Cmd for styling (`codeeditor/utils.ts:103`). Ctrl+Enter submit has its own listener (`common-form.ts:16`). Nothing has to move. |
| Unit tests need no browser | **Yes.** The test environment (happy-dom) correctly detects editable areas, the `?` key and keys another widget already handled; I checked with a throwaway script. One catch: unit tests run concurrently and share module state (`vitest.config.ts`: `isolate: false`, `concurrent: true`). The registry tests need `{concurrent: false}` plus a reset, as `aria-announce.test.ts:5-6` already does. |
| Alternative (a) "can't express a shortcut with no input to focus" | **Only for today's markup**, where a `<kbd>` sits next to an input. An attribute on any element (a link to click, a box to focus) could express it. |
| #57 "can't list shortcuts by searching the page" | **Doesn't hold.** The page's shortcuts are elements on the page, and hidden ones are still there. |
| A duplicate binding should throw | **Clashes with the design.** Clicking through the file tree reloads the `t` box (`ViewFileTreeStore.ts:45`), so `t` would register twice. |
| "GitHub's chord timeout is roughly a second" | **Doesn't hold.** The README of GitHub's own shortcut library gives 1500 ms. |

**New finding: a bug in the current code.** On a repo page, open the profile menu and press `s`. The menu jumps to "Starred", and then the global handler also moves the cursor to the code search. The cause is that the menu marks the key as handled (`aria-menu.ts:147-152`), but `shortcut.ts` never checks for that. `common-form.ts:19` already does that check. I found this by reading the code and haven't tried it in a browser. Once two-key shortcuts exist, typing `g` inside a menu would also start a `g` sequence.

**What this means for the design decision:** both of its arguments against alternative (a) are weak, so the rationale needs rewriting whichever way you go.

**What the tightened issue could look like:** it only touches `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts` plus a new `shortcut.test.ts`. No templates, Go, CSS or locale files change. That splits into about four commits:
1. Tests that pin down today's `s`, `t` and Escape behaviour, written against the current code.
2. The fix for keys a widget already handled.
3. Single-key shortcuts moved into the registry.
4. Two-key sequences.

The tests from commit 1 have to stay green through the later commits, so each refactor step shows it didn't break anything.

Four choices change what the draft says, so I need them from you first:

**Where should a shortcut be declared? This decides most of the rewritten ACs and the Design Decision.**

Options:
- **JS registry (Recommended)** - Keep #56's direction. Page code calls registerShortcut; the s/t <kbd>s register themselves when they load and look up their input at press time. #57, #59 and #60 are already written against a registry, and #58 stays a medium issue. Only the rationale needs rewriting.
- **Attribute on any element** - Alternative (a), widened: put data-shortcut-keys on any element; on a match, inputs are focused and links/buttons clicked. #58 would become a template-only change (risk: it shrinks to small), and #57, #59 and #60 need their design decisions rewritten.

**Which of these belong in #56? Anything left unticked goes to Out of Scope.** _(select multiple)_

Options:
- **Handled-key fix (Recommended)** - Skip keys a widget already handled (the profile-menu + s bug). One check, same as common-form.ts:19. Without it, typing g in a menu starts a g sequence.
- **Descriptions (Recommended)** - Each shortcut stores a short, already-translated description so #57 can list it; s/t reuse their input's placeholder text. If left out, #57 adds the field and edits every registration.
- **Duplicate check (Recommended)** - Registering the same keys twice fails loudly; a <kbd> that loads again during file-tree navigation is skipped instead of failing.
- **Modifier keys (mod+k)** - Nothing in #57–#60 uses one. Leaving it out keeps today's Ctrl/Alt/Cmd bail-out and removes the `mod` open question.

**After g, the user presses a key that doesn't finish any sequence, e.g. `g s`. What happens to s?**

Options:
- **Fresh press (Recommended)** - The unfinished g is dropped and s works as if g was never pressed. Same rule as the timeout case (AC3), so there's only one rule.
- **Swallow both** - Neither key does anything, so a typo never triggers a shortcut, but the user has to press s again.

**How long should the wait between the two keys of a sequence be?**

Options:
- **1500 ms (Recommended)** - What the old issue proposed, and what GitHub's shortcut library documents.
- **1000 ms** - Snappier, but slower typists may miss the window.

### User Story

As a front-end developer, I want one place to add keyboard shortcuts, including two-key sequences like `g c`, so that I can add a shortcut and have it listed in a help dialog without editing the page-wide key handler each time.

### User Scenario

Nothing changes for someone using Gitea: `s` still focuses the code search on a repository's home page, `t` still focuses "Go to file", and Escape still clears either box.

What changes is underneath. Today a shortcut can only be a `<kbd>` hint sitting next to a text box, and the key handler finds it by searching the page. After this issue, a front-end developer adds a shortcut with one call from their page code, giving its keys, a short description and what it does. Typing in a text box, two-key timing and keys that a menu has already used are handled for them.

| Today | After this issue |
| --- | --- |
| A shortcut must be a `<kbd>` hint next to a text box | Page code can add any shortcut; the `S` and `T` hints keep working as they are |
| Single keys only | Single keys and two-key sequences such as `g c` |
| Nothing on the page knows which shortcuts exist | Every shortcut has its keys and a description that a help dialog can list |

The issues that follow build on this: #57 lists the shortcuts in a `?` dialog, #58 adds the `g` sequences, #59 adds `c`, and #60 adds a way to turn them off.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given the repository home page, when the user presses `s` with focus outside a text field, then the code search box is focused and its `S` hint hides; `t` does the same for the "Go to file" box on file and folder views.
- [ ] AC2: Given focus is in a box that shows a shortcut hint, when the user presses Escape, then the box is cleared and loses focus, as it does today.
- [ ] AC3: Given a single-key shortcut such as `?` is added from code, when the user presses that key with focus outside a text field, then its action runs once and the key does nothing else.
- [ ] AC4: Given the two-key sequence `g c` is added, when the user presses `g` and then `c` within 1500 ms, then its action runs once and neither key runs a single-key shortcut of its own.
- [ ] AC5: Given the same sequence, when the user presses `g` and then waits longer than 1500 ms, or presses a key that does not finish any sequence, then the `g` is dropped and the second key acts as a fresh press.
- [ ] AC6: Given focus is in an input, textarea, select or editable area, when the user presses a key that has a shortcut, then no shortcut runs and the key types as normal.
- [ ] AC7: Given a menu or other widget has already used a key (for example a menu jumping to an item when the user types its first letter), when the key reaches the page, then no shortcut runs and any half-finished sequence is dropped.
- [ ] AC8: Given a shortcut already exists for some keys, when code adds the same keys again, or keys where one is the start of the other (a lone `g` and `g c`), then adding it fails with an error; an `S` or `T` hint that loads again, for example while moving through the file tree, is not an error and its key keeps working.
- [ ] AC9: Given the shortcuts on a page, when they are listed, then each one has its keys and a short translated description; `s` and `t` use their box's placeholder text ("Search code…" and "Go to file").

### Out of Scope

- Help dialog that lists the shortcuts, and grouping them into sections: Issue (#57)
- `g` navigation shortcuts: Issue (#58)
- `c` to focus the comment box: Issue (#59)
- Turning shortcuts off: Issue (#60)
- Shortcuts that use Ctrl, Alt or Cmd (e.g. Ctrl/Cmd+K). None of the planned shortcuts need one, so those presses keep being ignored, as they are today.
- Remapping shortcuts, or saving anything to the server.
- The code editor's and Markdown editor's own keys, which stay where they are.

### Open Questions

- ~~How long should the wait between the two keys of a sequence be?~~: **Answered: 1500 ms**, the same as GitHub's own shortcut library.
- ~~Should a `mod` key mean Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere?~~: **No longer applies**, since modifier keys are out of scope.

### Design Decisions

#### Decision 1: Shortcuts live in one list that page code adds to

**Decision:** Shortcuts are kept in one list, and a single page-wide key handler reads it. The `S` and `T` hints keep their current markup and add themselves to the list when they load.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Mark any element with its shortcut keys, and have the key handler focus or click whichever element matches. (b) Give each element its own key listener and drop the page-wide one.
**Rationale:** (a) can only focus or click an element, so a shortcut that does anything else, like `?` opening a dialog in #57, needs a hidden button made just to be clicked; #57, #59 and #60 are also already planned around a list. (b) breaks two-key sequences, because the first key arrives with focus on the page rather than on any one element.
**Consequences:** Adding a shortcut becomes one call, and #57 and #60 each have one place to look. The list is shared by the whole page, so its tests can't run at the same time as each other and need a way to empty it between cases. The page markup alone no longer shows every shortcut.

#### Decision 2: A `<kbd>` hint joins the list once and finds its box when pressed

**Decision:** The first `S` or `T` hint to load adds its key to the list, later copies of the same hint are skipped, and pressing the key looks up whichever box is on the page at that moment.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Each hint adds its own entry tied to its own box, as first proposed. (b) Leave the hints outside the list, and have the key handler check them after the list.
**Rationale:** Moving through the file tree replaces the part of the page that holds the "Go to file" box, so its `T` hint loads again. Under (a) that second load is a duplicate, and the old entry points at a box that no longer exists. (b) avoids that, but leaves two places a shortcut can come from, so #57 and #60 would both have to check both.
**Consequences:** The duplicate check has to tell a hint loading again apart from two pieces of code claiming the same keys; only the second is an error. If the box is gone when the key is pressed, nothing happens, as today.

#### Decision 3: An unfinished sequence is dropped and the next key counts on its own

**Decision:** If `g` is followed by a key that doesn't finish a sequence, or by nothing for 1500 ms, the `g` is forgotten and the next key is handled as a fresh press.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Ignore both keys. (b) Keep waiting for a valid second key until the 1500 ms are up, ignoring wrong keys in between.
**Rationale:** One rule covers both a slow and a wrong second key, and a `g` pressed by mistake costs nothing: `s` still focuses the search. (a) makes a typo cost an extra press, and (b) makes keys silently disappear for up to a second and a half.
**Consequences:** A slow `g c` runs whatever `c` does on its own, which on an issue page will be #59's comment box rather than the Code tab.

#### Decision 4: Descriptions are translated text handed in with the shortcut

**Decision:** Each shortcut is added with a short description that is already translated. The `S` and `T` hints use their box's placeholder text, which the server has already translated.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Store a translation key and look it up in the browser. (b) Leave descriptions out until #57 needs them.
**Rationale:** (a) isn't available: the browser side of Gitea only receives a small fixed set of translated strings, and anything else has to come with the page. (b) would mean #57 changes how every shortcut is added, including any that #58 and #59 have added by then.
**Consequences:** Whoever adds a shortcut has to get translated text from the page, for example from a tab's own label in #58. Grouping shortcuts into sections is left to #57.

### Scope

TITLE: Central keyboard-shortcut registry with chords and modifiers
UPDATED: 2026-10-16T14:15:30Z
LABELS: enhancement, scope: medium, Deferred  MILESTONE: none

## User Story

As a front-end developer, I want one place to add keyboard shortcuts, including two-key sequences like `g c`, so that I can add a shortcut and have it listed in a help dialog without editing the page-wide key handler each time.

## User Scenario
Nothing changes for the end user in this issue as all changes attempt to refactor code while keeping the current functionality intact; pressing `s` on a repository home page still focuses the sidebar search, and `t` on the code view still opens the file finder. Only underlying code will change, where a developer adding a shortcut now calls `registerShortcut()` instead of adding another branch to the global  `keydown` handler.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the repository home page, when the user presses `s` with focus outside a text field, then the code search box is focused and its `S` hint hides; `t` does the same for the "Go to file" box on file and folder views.
- [ ] AC2: Given focus is in a box that shows a shortcut hint, when the user presses Escape, then the box is cleared and loses focus, as it does today.
- [ ] AC3: Given a single-key shortcut such as `?` is added from code, when the user presses that key with focus outside a text field, then its action runs once and the key does nothing else.
- [ ] AC4: Given the two-key sequence `g c` is added, when the user presses `g` and then `c` within 1500 ms, then its action runs once and neither key runs a single-key shortcut of its own.
- [ ] AC5: Given the same sequence, when the user presses `g` and then waits longer than 1500 ms, or presses a key that does not finish any sequence, then the `g` is dropped and the second key acts as a fresh press.
- [ ] AC6: Given focus is in an input, textarea, select or editable area, when the user presses a key that has a shortcut, then no shortcut runs and the key types as normal.
- [ ] AC7: Given a menu or other widget has already used a key (for example a menu jumping to an item when the user types its first letter), when the key reaches the page, then no shortcut runs and any half-finished sequence is dropped.
- [ ] AC8: Given a shortcut already exists for some keys, when code adds the same keys again, or keys where one is the start of the other (a lone `g` and `g c`), then adding it fails with an error; an `S` or `T` hint that loads again, for example while moving through the file tree, is not an error and its key keeps working.
- [ ] AC9: Given the shortcuts on a page, when they are listed, then each one has its keys and a short translated description; `s` and `t` use their box's placeholder text ("Search codeM-bM-^@M-&" and "Go to file").

## Out of Scope
- Help dialog that lists the shortcuts, and grouping them into sections: Issue (#57)
- `g` navigation shortcuts: Issue (#58)
- `c` to focus the comment box: Issue (#59)
- Turning shortcuts off: Issue (#60)
- Shortcuts that use Ctrl, Alt or Cmd (e.g. Ctrl/Cmd+K). None of the planned shortcuts need one, so those presses keep being ignored, as they are today.
- Remapping shortcuts by the user, or saving anything to the server.
- The code editor's and Markdown editor's own keys, which stay where they are.

### Open Questions
None

#23 author=Jack-Donohue assignees= milestone=none created=2026-09-15T01:22:31Z labels=scope: large
-----#12
Let users choose a reason when closing an issue or pull request [CLOSED] assignees=ab-wm

## Summary
In Gitea, a closed issue or pull request is simply "closed" — there's no way to tell whether it was fixed, rejected, a duplicate, or closed for some other reason. Maintainers end up writing "closing as duplicate of #12" in comments, and anyone browsing closed items later can't tell finished work from abandoned ideas.

This feature adds a **close reason** to issues and pull requests. The reason is chosen when closing, saved in the database, and shown on the issue/PR and in its timeline. Preset reasons cover the common cases, and an **Other** option lets the user type a custom reason. Items closed automatically (by a commit, a merged PR, a deleted branch, etc.) get a sensible reason too.

This helps maintainers triage faster, and helps contributors and project managers read a project's history accurately — for example, how much was actually completed versus declined.

## User story
As a repository maintainer, I want to choose why I'm closing an issue or pull request — from a list or by typing my own reason — so that anyone reading it later knows what happened without digging through comments.

## Proposed behavior

### Closing manually (web UI)
- The **Close** button on issues becomes a split button with a dropdown:
  - **Close as completed** (default)
  - **Close as not planned**
  - **Close as duplicate** — asks for the original issue number (e.g. `#12`)
  - **Close with other reason…** — shows a text box for a custom reason (required when chosen, max 255 characters)
- The **Close pull request** button gets the same dropdown **without "Completed"**, since a finished PR is *merged*, not closed. Options: **Not planned** (default), **Duplicate**, **Other…**. Merging stays a separate state and needs no reason.
- The **issue/PR list** bulk "Close" action offers the same reason choice (preset reasons only; one reason applied to all selected items).

### Saving and display
- A database migration adds to the `issue` table (which also stores PRs):
  - `close_reason` — `completed`, `not_planned`, `duplicate`, or `other`
  - `close_reason_text` — the custom text when the reason is `other`
  - `duplicate_of_id` — the original issue/PR when the reason is `duplicate`
- The same fields are stored on the close timeline comment, so every close/reopen in the history keeps its own reason.
- The timeline shows e.g. "closed this as not planned", "closed this as a duplicate of #12", or "closed this: *custom text*".
- Custom text is displayed as plain text (escaped, not rendered as Markdown/HTML).
- Closed items show a distinct icon/label per reason (e.g. "not planned" looks different from "completed").
- **Reopening** clears the current reason (the old reason stays visible in the timeline).
- Existing closed issues/PRs have no reason and display exactly as they do today.

### Automatic closing

| How it closes | Code path | Reason saved |
|---|---|---|
| Commit message keyword ("fixes #5") | `services/issue/commit.go` | Completed |
| Merged PR that references an issue | `services/pull/merge.go` | Completed (on the referenced issue) |
| PR auto-closed because its head branch was deleted | `services/pull/pull.go` (`AdjustPullsCausedByBranchDeleted`) | Not planned |
| PRs auto-closed because the repo's branches were removed | `services/pull/pull.go` (`CloseRepoBranchesPulls`) | Not planned |
| API call that closes without giving a reason | `routers/api/v1/repo/issue.go` | Completed (issues) / Not planned (PRs) |

### API
- Issue and pull request edit endpoints accept optional `close_reason` (`completed`, `not_planned`, `duplicate`, `other`), `close_reason_text`, and `duplicate_of` fields.
- Issue and PR JSON responses include `close_reason` and `close_reason_text` (similar to GitHub's `state_reason`).
- Invalid combinations are rejected with 422 (e.g. `other` with empty text, `duplicate` pointing at a nonexistent issue, `completed` on a PR).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A database migration adds the close-reason columns; existing issues and PRs are unaffected.
- [ ] Users can pick a preset reason or type a custom one when closing an issue or PR from its page.
- [ ] PRs do not offer "Completed"; merging still works without a reason.
- [ ] The bulk close action on issue/PR lists lets users pick a preset reason.
- [ ] "Duplicate" requires a valid issue/PR number in the same repository, and the timeline links to it.
- [ ] "Other" requires non-empty text (≤ 255 chars), which is saved and displayed escaped.
- [ ] Timeline and closed-item display show the reason; all new UI strings are in `locale_en-US.json`.
- [ ] Each automatic close path saves the reason listed in the table above.
- [ ] Reopening clears the current reason but keeps it in the timeline history.
```

**What a category needs to be:** just a short label saying which section a shortcut belongs to, such as `repo` or `issue`, stored with the shortcut. Turning that label into a translated heading like "Repository" is display work, and that part is genuinely #57's.

**Your options:**

1. **Optional section label in #56 (my recommendation).** #56 accepts the label when a shortcut is added and returns it when the shortcuts are listed. It doesn't display or translate it.
   - `s` and `t` get `repo`, set in the same code #56 already changes.
   - #58 and #59 pass their label when they add their shortcuts.
   - #57 only turns labels into headings, so nobody edits anyone else's code later.
   - It also shrinks the fallout: #57 AC5 needs no change, and only AC6 does.
2. **#57 adds it later.** #57 would have to change #56's code and every shortcut that exists by then: `s`, `t`, and #58's and #59's shortcuts if those merge first. That's the cross-issue refactor you're worried about.
3. **No sections at all.** #57 shows one flat list of about ten shortcuts. It's the least code, but it changes #57's spec (scenario line 10 and AC5), and #57 isn't your issue.

Taking #57 yourself would be the scope creep. It's another medium issue on top of your two, just to avoid adding one field.

**If you pick option 1, the #56 edits are:**
- **AC9:** add "and, if given, a section label; `s` and `t` are in the repository section".
- **Out of Scope:** change "grouping them into sections" to "turning section labels into headings".

The #57 list then shrinks to the AC6 change only. #59 AC5 stays as I listed it, because it also depends on #57 existing at all, not just on categories.

**When a repo uses an external issue tracker or wiki, the tab opens another site in a new tab. What should g i / g w do?**

<!--
Draft for the #58 issue body. Edit before posting.
Suggested title: `g` navigation shortcuts for repository tabs and notifications
-->

## User Story

As a Gitea user who knows GitHub's keyboard shortcuts, I want the same two-key `g` shortcuts to take me to a repository's code, issues, pull requests, actions and wiki, and to my notifications, so that I can move around without reaching for the mouse.

## User Scenario
A reviewer is reading a file on a feature branch. They press `g` then `i` and land on the repository's issue list, then `g` then `p` for the pull request list. Pressing `g` then `c` takes them back to the repository's front page on its default branch, the same as on GitHub. From anywhere in Gitea, while signed in, `g` then `n` opens their notifications.

A shortcut only works when its tab is shown. On a repository with the wiki turned off, or one that uses an external wiki, pressing `g` then `w` does nothing at all: no navigation, no error.

| Keys | Goes to | Works when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `g c` | The repository's front page, default branch | The Code tab is shown |
| `g i` | Issues | Gitea's own issue tracker is shown |
| `g p` | Pull requests | The Pull requests tab is shown |
| `g a` | Actions | The Actions tab is shown |
| `g w` | Wiki | Gitea's own wiki is shown |
| `g n` | Notifications | The user is signed in (any page) |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a page inside a repository, when the user presses `g` then `i`, `p`, `a` or `w`, then the browser goes to that repository's Issues, Pull requests, Actions or Wiki tab.
- [ ] AC2: Given a page inside a repository while browsing a branch other than the default, when the user presses `g` then `c`, then the browser goes to the repository's front page on its default branch.
- [ ] AC3: Given a tab that is not shown (its unit is disabled, the user cannot read it, or the repository is empty), when the user presses its shortcut, then nothing happens and the page does not navigate.
- [ ] AC4: Given a repository that uses an external issue tracker or an external wiki, when the user presses `g i` or `g w`, then nothing happens and the browser never leaves Gitea.
- [ ] AC5: Given a narrow window where some tabs have moved into the tab bar's "more" menu, when the user presses one of their shortcuts, then it still works.
- [ ] AC6: Given any page while signed in, when the user presses `g` then `n`, then the browser goes to the notifications page; when signed out, nothing happens.
- [ ] AC7: Given a page outside any repository, when the user presses a repository shortcut such as `g i`, then nothing happens.
- [ ] AC8: Given the shortcuts on a page, when they are listed, then each repository shortcut is described by its tab's translated name (for example "Issues", without the open count) and is in the repository section, and `g n` is "Notifications" in the site-wide section.

## Out of Scope
- GitHub shortcuts for tabs Gitea does not have: Discussions (`g g`) and Security (`g s`).
- Shortcuts for tabs GitHub has no shortcut for: Releases, Projects, Packages, Activity and Settings.
- Other site-wide shortcuts, such as GitHub's `s` or `/` to focus the top search bar.
- Shortcuts that act on the current page instead of navigating, such as closing an issue or assigning labels.
- Showing the shortcuts to the user: Issue (#57)
- Changing what the tab bar shows or where its tabs link.

## Open Questions
None

## Design Decisions
Below

## Scope
medium (5 points)

## AI Disclosure
Used claude-code for the drafting of this issue, followed by my changes and proofing.
