# #58 rewrite — notes (not for posting)

Draft body: `issue-58-draft.md`. Original body saved as `58.before.md`. Nothing applied to GitHub.

## Choices made (2026-10-16)

- Match GitHub, nothing more: repository `g c`, `g i`, `g p`, `g a`, `g w`, plus site-wide `g n`. GitHub's other repository shortcuts (`g g` Discussions, `g s` Security) have no Gitea tab. GitHub's docs do not list `g b` (Projects) or `g d` (dashboard); I wrongly said `g b` was GitHub's in the question.
- External tracker or wiki: no shortcut.
- `g c` goes to the front page on the default branch, as GitHub's Code tab does (checked on a live GitHub branch page: the Code tab links to `/owner/repo`). Reason: until #57 ships, nothing tells a user what `g c` does, so GitHub's behaviour is what they will expect.
- Help-dialog AC (old AC6) dropped. #57 needs no new AC: its AC1 lists every shortcut that was added, and #58 only adds shortcuts for tabs that exist.

## Claims in the old #58, checked

| Claim | Holds? |
| --- | --- |
| The tab bar only shows tabs the user may see | Yes: each tab is behind a permission or unit check (`templates/repo/header.tmpl:86-176`); empty repos also hide Actions, Releases and Activity |
| "No link, no shortcut" gives AC3/AC4 for free | Mostly; the exception is the external tracker or wiki, whose tab links off-site in a new tab (`header.tmpl:100-104`, `156-160`). Now AC4 |
| "Any page inside a repository" | Yes: only create, migrate and fork pages lack the tab bar |
| `g c` goes to "the code tab" | On a non-default branch the Code tab links to that branch (`header.tmpl:87`); the front page link is the repo name (`header.tmpl:9`). Now AC2 |
| Alternative (a) "would get sub-path installs wrong" | Doesn't hold: page code has `window.config.appSubUrl` (`templates/base/head_script.tmpl:11`). Its real cost is repeating the permission checks. Matters when you write the Design Decision |
| Coupled to the tab bar's markup | Holds. Narrow windows move tabs into a popup that stays inside `<overflow-menu>` (`webcomponents/overflow-menu.ts:184`). Now AC5 |
| AC7 "against a fixture repository" | E2E tests create repos through the API (`tests/e2e/utils.ts:43`); there are no fixtures |

## What changed from the old #58

- Title: "repo and global pages" now means exactly `g n` for global.
- Letter set: `g r` (Releases) dropped, `g w` added to the ACs (it was only in the scenario).
- New ACs: `g c` target (AC2), external tracker/wiki (AC4), narrow window (AC5), `g n` (AC6), descriptions and sections (AC8, from #56 AC9).
- AC3 widened from "issue unit disabled" to any tab that isn't shown.
- Dropped: the help-dialog AC (old AC6); the comment-box AC (old AC5), which #56 AC6 already covers (the e2e test can still check it); the Playwright AC (old AC7), since the test strategy goes in the PR, as in #56.
- Out of Scope: "Changing the repository navigation markup itself" became "Changing what the tab bar shows or where its tabs link", so it doesn't rule out an approach before you've picked one.
- Header line ("P2 — only if capacity allows") and the old footer dropped; Design Decisions left as "Below", as in #56.

## Things to know while implementing (not for the issue)

- Each tab's text includes its open count ("Issues 12"); AC8 wants the name only.
- The bell link is rendered twice (mobile and desktop, `templates/base/head_navbar.tmpl:10,65`) and only when signed in (`head_navbar_icons.tmpl:3`). Its visible text is just the count; the translated name is in `data-tooltip-content`.
- A slow `g c` on an issue page runs `c` on its own, which will be #59's comment box (#56's fresh-press rule).
- E2E setup: `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}` can set `has_issues: false`, `has_wiki: false`, `external_tracker` and `external_wiki` (`modules/structs/repo.go:186-198`); the existing helper only creates repos. AC5 needs a narrow viewport, AC6 a signed-out page.
- Tech debt to expect for the PR: the shortcuts depend on the tab bar's markup (Introduced); the tab-bar coupling is what the e2e test guards.

Honestly, it's medium mainly because of the testing work, not because of the feature code.

**The feature code is small.** It's one new piece of page code, roughly 40–70 lines, that finds the tabs and the bell link and adds six shortcuts through #56's list. That's lighter than #56, which has the sequence timing, the duplicate rules and a refactor that has to stay green. It's far lighter than your #53.

**The real work is the edge cases and proving them.** Each AC guards a real failure, not padding: a shortcut taking users off-site, shortcuts breaking silently in a narrow window, the bell being missing when signed out. Each one needs its own e2e setup, and only `apiCreateRepo` exists today. You'd have to add:
- a second branch, for `g c`;
- API calls that turn off issues and the wiki, and that set an external tracker and wiki;
- a narrow viewport;
- a signed-out page.

Plus unit tests for reading the tabs. Tests are 5 of the 20 PR points, so that work counts.

The course doesn't define small, medium or large; sizing is relative, by planning poker. In those terms I'd put #56 at 5 and #58 at about 3. "Medium" is defensible, but it sits at the small end, mostly on the strength of the test setup.

The Sprint 2 rule for CSCI 435 is "at least 2 medium issues (or equivalent points)", so it's about total points rather than labels. That gives you two options:

- **Keep #58 at medium.** That's defensible. If a reviewer or the instructor questions it, point to the e2e setup.
- **Add margin by taking #59.** #59 (`c` focuses the comment box, 2 points) is small, unowned and built on the same list. It's extra work, though, so only take it if you want the cushion.

I wouldn't add more to #58 itself. The ACs already cover everything GitHub's version does, and anything more would be the padding you were asking about.

> Sub-issue of #23 · **P3 — Sprint 2 carryover** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56

## User Story
As a user replying to an issue, I want a single key to jump to the comment box from anywhere on
the page, so that I do not have to scroll to the bottom or Tab through every comment to start
writing.

## User Scenario
A maintainer reads a long issue thread. Instead of scrolling past forty comments, they press `c`.
The page scrolls the comment editor into view and the cursor is in it. They type, realise they
want to re-read something, and press Escape — focus leaves the editor, the text they typed is
still there, and the page has not moved.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given an issue page with a comment editor, when the user presses `c` with focus on the
      document body, then the comment textarea is focused and scrolled into view.
- [ ] AC2: Given the comment editor is focused with text in it, when the user presses Escape, then
      the editor is blurred and its content is left unchanged.
- [ ] AC3: Given an archived repository or a signed-out visitor, where no comment editor is
      rendered, when the user presses `c`, then nothing happens and no error is logged.
- [ ] AC4: Given focus is already inside the comment editor, when the user types `c`, then a
      literal `c` is inserted.
- [ ] AC5: A Playwright test covers AC1, AC2 and AC4.

## Out of Scope
- The pull request review comment boxes and the inline diff reply boxes.
- Submitting the comment — `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+Enter already does that via
  `initGlobalEnterQuickSubmit` in `web_src/js/features/common-form.ts` and is not touched here.
- Quote-reply (`r` on GitHub) and any other issue-page action key.

#59 is the smallest of the three in code, but the per-issue course work around it is about as big as the code itself.

**Code: small**
- **The `c` shortcut:** a few lines in the issue page code. When pressed, it finds the comment box, focuses it and scrolls it into view. The comment box already has a focus method that works in both editor modes, including the legacy editor some users switch to (`ComboMarkdownEditor.ts:399-408`), so you'd use that instead of focusing the text area directly.
- **Escape to leave the box:** a few more lines. There's no clash with the mention/emoji suggestion popup: when that popup is open, it handles Escape itself and stops the key there (`@github/text-expander-element`, `onKeydown`). So Escape closes the popup first, and only a second Escape leaves the box.
- **Translated description:** #56 requires one, so the comment form needs one attribute with a translated label. That's a one-line template change, plus a locale key if no existing one fits.
- **In total:** probably 30–50 lines of TypeScript and a line of template.

**Tests: easier than #58**
- The e2e helpers already exist: `apiCreateRepo` and `apiCreateIssue` (`tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` uses both). AC1, AC2 and AC4 each need just one repo with one issue.
- AC3 ("no comment box, nothing happens") is a unit test.

**Course overhead: the part people underestimate**
- **Spec:** take #59 and add it to the milestone. Rewrite the spec in your own voice, as you did for #56 and #58, since D2 is graded individually. Then get a teammate's "Spec reviewed".
- **Decisions:** at least one design decision with two alternatives.
- **PR:** its own branch and PR, with the tech debt section, a reviewer and a review rubric.
- **AI log:** its own AI Assistance comment and log on the issue.

**Totals:** #56 ≈ 5, #58 ≈ 3, #59 ≈ 2, which makes 10. That covers "two medium or equivalent points" even with my stricter #58 estimate. #59 is only blocked by #56, so you could build it alongside #58 once #56 merges.

Whether the cushion is worth an extra spec, PR and review cycle is your call. On code alone it's an afternoon-sized issue.

async function tryOnQuoteReply(e: Event) {
  const clickTarget = (e.target as HTMLElement).closest('.quote-reply');
  if (!clickTarget) return;

  e.preventDefault();
  const contentToQuoteId = clickTarget.getAttribute('data-target');
  const targetRawToQuote = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`#${contentToQuoteId}.raw-content`)!;
  const targetMarkupToQuote = targetRawToQuote.parentElement!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.render-content.markup')!;
  let contentToQuote = extractSelectedMarkdown(targetMarkupToQuote);
  if (!contentToQuote) contentToQuote = targetRawToQuote.textContent;
  const quotedContent = `${contentToQuote.replace(/^/mg, '> ')}\n\n`;

  let editor;
  if (clickTarget.classList.contains('quote-reply-diff')) {
    const replyBtn = clickTarget.closest('.comment-code-cloud')!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('button.comment-form-reply')!;
    editor = await handleReply(replyBtn);
  } else {
    // for normal issue/comment page
    editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(document.querySelector('#comment-form .combo-markdown-editor'))!;
  }

  if (editor.value()) {
    editor.value(`${editor.value()}\n\n${quotedContent}`);
  } else {
    editor.value(quotedContent);
  }
  editor.focus();
  editor.moveCursorToEnd();

function isTextExpanderShown(textarea: HTMLElement): boolean {
  return Boolean(textarea.closest('text-expander')?.querySelector('.suggestions'));
}

export function initTextareaMarkdown(textarea: HTMLTextAreaElement) {
  textarea.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    if (isTextExpanderShown(textarea)) return;
    if (e.key === 'Tab' && !e.ctrlKey && !e.metaKey && !e.altKey) {
      // use Tab/Shift-Tab to indent/unindent the selected lines
      handleIndentSelection(textarea, e);
    } else if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey && !e.ctrlKey && !e.metaKey && !e.altKey) {
      // use Enter to insert a new line with the same indention and prefix
      handleNewline(textarea, e);
    } else if (pairs.has(e.key)) {
      handlePairCharacter(textarea, e);
    }
  });
}

**GitHub has no 'focus the comment box' key; its nearest is r (quote selected text into your reply). Which should #59 be?**

Options:
- **GitHub's r (Recommended)** - Select text in a comment, press r: it's quoted into the reply box and the cursor goes there. Reuses Gitea's existing Quote reply action, matches GitHub and #23's goal. The user story changes from 'jump to the box' to 'quote into my reply'.
- **Keep c** - Focus the reply box, as written today. A Gitea-only key with no GitHub precedent; GitHub users know c as 'create issue' on lists.
- **Both r and c** - Quote with r, jump with c. Covers both stories, but grows the issue.

<!--
Draft for the #59 issue body. Edit before posting.
Suggested title: `r` quotes selected text into the reply box on issue and pull request pages
-->

## User Story

As a user replying on an issue or pull request, I want GitHub's `r` shortcut to quote the text I have selected into my reply, or take me straight to the reply box when nothing is selected, so that I can answer a specific point without scrolling to the bottom or opening the comment's menu.

## User Scenario
A maintainer is reading a long issue thread. They select a sentence in someone's comment and press `r`. The page scrolls to the reply box at the bottom, the sentence is already in it as a Markdown quote, and the cursor sits after it, ready to type. Later, back at the top of the thread with nothing selected, they press `r` again and land in the same reply box with their text still there.

On a page with no reply box, such as an archived repository or when signed out, `r` does nothing.

| When the user presses `r` with | `r` does |
| --- | --- |
| Text selected inside one comment | Quotes it into the reply box and puts the cursor after it |
| Nothing selected, or a selection that is not inside a single comment | Jumps to the reply box |
| No reply box on the page | Nothing |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given text is selected inside a comment or the issue description on an issue or pull request page, when the user presses `r`, then the text is added to the reply box as a Markdown quote, the box scrolls into view, and the cursor is placed after the quote.
- [ ] AC2: Given the reply box already has text in it, when the user quotes with `r`, then the existing text is kept and the quote is added after it.
- [ ] AC3: Given nothing is selected, or the selection is not inside a single comment, when the user presses `r`, then the reply box scrolls into view with the cursor in it and its text unchanged.
- [ ] AC4: Given the reply box is showing its Preview tab, when the user presses `r`, then it switches back to Write so the cursor and any quote can be seen.
- [ ] AC5: Given a page with no reply box (an archived repository, a signed-out visitor, or a locked conversation the user cannot comment on), when the user presses `r`, then nothing happens and no error is logged.
- [ ] AC6: Given a page where `r` works, when the shortcuts are listed, then `r` is described by the translated "Quote reply" label and is in the issue section.

## Out of Scope
- Comments in code-review threads and their own reply boxes.
- GitHub's other issue page shortcuts (`a`, `l`, `m`, `q` and `x`), and its `c` for "Create an issue" on issue lists.
- Escape to leave the reply box; Tab already leaves it.
- Submitting the comment: `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+Enter already does that and is not touched here.
- Changes to the "Quote reply" item in each comment's menu.
- Showing the shortcuts to the user: Issue (#57)

## Open Questions
None

## Design Decisions
Below

## Scope
small (2 points)

## AI Disclosure
Used claude-code for the drafting of this issue, followed by my changes and proofing.

# #59 rewrite — notes (not for posting)

Draft body: `issue-59-draft.md`. Original body saved as `59.before.md`. Nothing applied to GitHub.

## Choices made (2026-10-16)

- GitHub's `r` instead of `c`: GitHub has no "focus the comment box" key; its `c` means "Create an issue" on lists, and its `r` quotes the selected text into your reply.
- With nothing selected, `r` jumps to the reply box. This keeps the original #59 story, and goes slightly beyond what GitHub documents.
- Escape-to-leave (old AC2) dropped: not GitHub behaviour, and Tab already leaves the box (it only indents when text is selected, `web_src/js/features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts:35`).

## Claims in the old #59, checked

| Claim | Holds? |
| --- | --- |
| Works "on issue and PR pages" | The title said both, AC1 only issues. Both use the same form (`templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl:83`); a PR's Files changed tab has no main reply box |
| AC3: no comment box when archived or signed out | Incomplete: a locked conversation also hides it from users without write access (`view_content.tmpl:76`). Now AC5 |
| "The comment textarea is focused" | The box can be in the legacy editor or on its Preview tab; the editor's own focus handles the legacy mode (`features/comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts:399-405`), but nothing switches back from Preview. Now AC4 |
| Design (a): a `<kbd>` hint is the wrong cue | Holds, and #56 AC2 adds a stronger reason: Escape clears any box with a hint, which would wipe a half-written comment |
| Design (b): the editor is rendered lazily in several places | Weak: the main reply box is in the page from the start; only the editor attached to it starts after load. Edit boxes are created on demand, but those are out of scope |
| Ctrl/Cmd+Enter via `initGlobalEnterQuickSubmit` | Yes (`features/common-form.ts:15`) |

## What changed from the old #59

- Key and story: `c` → `r`, "jump to the box" → "quote into my reply, or jump to the box".
- New ACs: appending to existing text (AC2), no selection (AC3), Preview tab (AC4), description and section (AC6, from #56 AC9).
- AC5 widened with locked conversations.
- Dropped: Escape (old AC2); typing `r` in a text field (old AC4), which #56 AC6 covers (the e2e test can still check it); the Playwright AC, since the test strategy goes in the PR as in #56 and #58.
- Header line and old Design Decision dropped; Design Decisions left as "Below".

## Things to know while implementing (not for the issue)

- Gitea already has the quote logic: "Quote reply" in each comment's "…" menu (`templates/repo/issue/view_content/context_menu.tmpl:18`), handled by `tryOnQuoteReply` (`features/repo-issue-edit.ts:123-150`), wired through a page-wide click listener (`:154-156`). With no selection the menu quotes the whole comment; `r` jumps instead (AC3).
- "Inside a single comment" is the existing rule: `extractSelectedMarkdown` only returns text when the whole selection sits in that comment (`repo-issue-edit.ts:113`).
- The main reply box is found with `getComboMarkdownEditor(document.querySelector('#comment-form .combo-markdown-editor'))` (`repo-issue-edit.ts:141`); `switchTabToEditor()` (`ComboMarkdownEditor.ts:290`) leaves Preview.
- Existing bug, found by reading the code and not tried: on a locked conversation, a user without write access still sees "Quote reply" in the menu (`context_menu.tmpl:14-18`), but there is no reply box, so clicking it hits a missing editor (`repo-issue-edit.ts:141-144`). If `r` reuses that path, AC5 needs a guard there, which also fixes the menu item. Either way it is "Encountered" tech debt for the PR.
- The translated "Quote reply" label (`repo.issues.context.quote_reply`) is on the page whenever the menu is (signed in, not archived).
- E2E: `apiCreateRepo` and `apiCreateIssue` exist (`tests/e2e/utils.ts`, used in `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts`).

## Size

#56 ≈ 5, #58 = 3 (as posted), #59 ≈ 2, for 10 in total.

wait, why exactly we are completely dropping the c. Is c just completely unused in github?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-16 15:27:46Z)**_

No, GitHub does use `c`, just not on issue or PR pages. From GitHub's shortcut docs:

- **On the issue and pull request lists,** `c` means "Create an issue".
- **On a PR's "Files changed" tab,** `c` opens the "Commits" dropdown to pick which commits the diff shows.
- **On an issue or PR page itself** (the conversation), GitHub binds nothing to `c`.

`c` was dropped for two reasons:

1. **`r` already does its job.** With nothing selected, `r` jumps to the reply box, which was everything the old `c` did. A `c` that focuses the box would just be a second key for the same action.
2. **It would give `c` a meaning GitHub doesn't have.** It wouldn't clash on the issue page itself, since GitHub leaves `c` unused there. But someone who knows GitHub thinks of `c` as "create", and under your "match GitHub" rule a made-up meaning is what you were avoiding.

Leaving `c` unused keeps it free for GitHub's own meaning later. "`c` creates an issue from the issue list" would fit the "no link, no shortcut" pattern from #58 (click the list's "New issue" button), and it's small. It's a different feature from #59's story, though, so it belongs under #23 as future work rather than inside #59.

If you'd still rather have `c` jump to the box as well, that's the "Both r and c" option. It's cheap in code, but it adds a Gitea-only key that does the same thing as `r` with no selection.

    async toggleMenu() {

      if (!this.commits.length && this.menuVisible && !this.isLoading) {
        this.isLoading = true;
        try {
          await this.fetchCommits();
        } finally {
          this.isLoading = false;
        }
      }
      // set correct tabindex to allow easier navigation
      this.$nextTick(() => {
        if (this.menuVisible) {
          this.focusElem(this.$refs.showAllChanges as HTMLElement, this.$refs.expandBtn as HTMLElement);
        } else {
          this.focusElem(this.$refs.expandBtn as HTMLElement, this.$refs.showAllChanges as HTMLElement);
        }
      });
    },

<!--
Draft for the #59 issue body. Edit before posting.
Suggested title: GitHub's `c` shortcuts for the issue and pull request lists and the pull request commit picker
-->

## User Story

As a Gitea user who knows GitHub's keyboard shortcuts, I want `c` to do what it does on GitHub, starting a new issue or pull request from the list and opening the commit picker on a pull request's changed files, so that I can start new work or narrow a review without reaching for the mouse.

## User Scenario
A maintainer triaging a repository's issue list presses `c` and lands on the new issue page, or on the template chooser when the repository has issue templates, exactly as if they had clicked "New Issue". On the pull request list, `c` opens the new pull request page in the same way.

Later, reviewing a pull request's "Files changed" tab, they press `c`. The commit picker opens with its first entry focused; the arrow keys move through the commits and Escape closes it, as they do after clicking it. On an archived repository, where there is nothing to create, `c` on the lists does nothing.

| Page | `c` does | Works when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Issue list | Same as clicking "New Issue" | The "New Issue" button is shown |
| Pull request list | Same as clicking "New Pull Request" | The "New Pull Request" button is shown and enabled |
| A pull request's "Files changed" tab | Opens the commit picker | Always on that tab |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a repository's issue list, when the user presses `c`, then the browser goes where the "New Issue" button leads: the new issue page, or the template chooser when the repository has issue templates.
- [ ] AC2: Given a repository's pull request list, when the user presses `c`, then the browser goes where the "New Pull Request" button leads.
- [ ] AC3: Given a list whose create button is missing or disabled (for example an archived repository, whose pull request list shows "Compare commits" instead), when the user presses `c`, then nothing happens.
- [ ] AC4: Given a pull request's "Files changed" tab, when the user presses `c`, then the commit picker opens with focus on its first entry, and the arrow keys and Escape work as they do after clicking it.
- [ ] AC5: Given any other page, such as an issue's own page or the compare page, when the user presses `c`, then nothing happens.
- [ ] AC6: Given a page where `c` works, when the shortcuts are listed, then `c` is described by the translated label of what it opens ("New Issue", "New Pull Request" or "Filter by commit"), and is in the issue section on the lists and the pull request section on the "Files changed" tab.

## Out of Scope
- Quoting a reply with `r`: a separate issue, to be created.
- `c` on other lists: milestone pages, and the site-wide or organisation Issues and Pull requests pages.
- GitHub's other list shortcuts (`u`, `l`, `m`, `a`, `o` and `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`/`).
- Changing the create buttons or the commit picker themselves.
- Showing the shortcuts to the user: Issue (#57)

## Open Questions
None

## Design Decisions
Below

## Scope
small (2 points)

# #59 rewrite — notes (not for posting)

Draft body: `issue-59-draft.md`. Original body saved as `59.before.md`. Nothing applied to GitHub.
The earlier `r` version is kept as `r-quote-reply-draft.md` and `r-quote-reply-notes.md`, for a new issue someone else can take.

## Choices made (2026-10-16)

- #59 becomes GitHub's `c` shortcuts, the same letter-based grouping as #58's `g`. The old "c focuses the comment box" was a Gitea-only meaning.
- Both of GitHub's meanings of `c`: "Create an issue" on the issue and PR lists, and opening the "Commits" dropdown on a PR's Files changed tab.
- On the PR list, `c` opens "New Pull Request" (the list's own button), so `c` always means "create one of these".
- `r` (quote reply, plus jumping to the box when nothing is selected) moves to a new issue; you don't mind someone else doing it.

## Where things are

| Shortcut | Target | Shown when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Issue list `c` | "New Issue" button, to `/issues/new` or `/issues/new/choose` (`templates/repo/issue/list.tmpl:24`) | Repository not archived |
| PR list `c` | "New Pull Request" button (`list.tmpl:27`), marked `disabled` when a PR can't be created | Repository not archived; an archived repo shows "Compare commits" with the same `issue-list-new` class instead (`list.tmpl:32`), which `c` must not use |
| Files changed `c` | The commit picker's button (`web_src/js/components/DiffCommitSelector.vue:220-227`), mounted on `#diff-commit-select` | Only on a PR's Files changed tab (`templates/repo/diff/box.tmpl:37-38`, `.PageIsPullFiles`) |

- Clicking the picker's button already loads the commits and focuses "Show all changes"; arrows and Escape are handled by the component (`DiffCommitSelector.vue`, `toggleMenu` and `onKeyDown`). So AC4 is "click the button"; no new picker code.
- Labels for AC6 are already translated on the page: `repo.issues.new` "New Issue", `repo.pulls.new` "New Pull Request", `repo.pulls.filter_changes_by_commit` "Filter by commit" (the picker button's `aria-label`).
- The milestone page has its own "New Issue" button (`templates/repo/issue/milestone_issues.tmpl:20`); it's out of scope, since GitHub doesn't document `c` there.

## Things to know while implementing (not for the issue)

- A slow `g c` on a list page will run `c` on its own and open "New Issue" (#56's fresh-press rule), just as a slow `g c` on an issue page would have hit the comment box before.
- Pressing `c` again while the picker is open is unspecified: the picker doesn't use the key, so it would reach the shortcut and click the button again (closing it). Decide whether that's fine when you write the decisions.
- Signed out: the list buttons are still shown, so `c` goes where the button goes (the sign-in page).
- E2E: `apiCreateRepo` exists; a PR for the Files changed test needs a branch with a commit and a PR, which the existing helpers don't create yet (check `tests/e2e/utils.ts` and `tests/e2e/pr-review.test.ts` for a pattern).

## Size

#56 ≈ 5, #58 = 3, #59 ≈ 2 (the lists are tiny; the picker is a button click plus its e2e setup), for 10 in total.
